title: Oakmont Financial — Activation intake + data handshake
summary: Kickoff to align on onboarding milestones, data ingestion approach, security requirements (KMS, audit logs, SSO), and a timeline for a 30-day pilot. Agreed next steps: runbook + security pack to be shared, schedule data ingest workshop, and a performance benchmark window. Several minor transcription errors; audio quality medium.
topics: Security: KMS, SOC2 evidence, audit logs, SSO/SAML
Network: VPC peering, egress, firewall rules
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Ortega: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you carving time out. Quick intros — I'm Maya, I'm your AE on the account. Ben is our solutions engineer, Renee is your CSM.
[00:18] Priya Shah: Hi all, Priya here — Head of AI at Oakmont. We've got Tom, Lena and Aaron on from infra and security.
[00:25] Ben Cho: Great, thanks. The goal for today is to align on the onboarding path, confirm what data you'll bring, and identify any blockers for a private deployment — or if you want to start hosted then move to dedicated.
[00:40] Tom Reeves: We're leaning toward private deployment — due to regs — but we want to understand the lift. Also curious about the dedicated pool option you mentioned in the docs.
[00:51] Maya Ortega: Yup. High-level: hosted is fastest to start; dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity with predictable latency. Private (VPC) is what most regulated financials pick — that's where we run a customer-controlled network with our private control plane.
[01:10] Lena Morales: Security is primary for us. We need KMS integration, audit logs surfaced into our SIEM, and SSO via SAML. Also data retention controls.
[01:22] Ben Cho: We support KMS/HSM integrations and can push audit logs to your syslog or an S3 bucket you control. Small note: there's sometimes a mismatch in auto transcribed docs where "K V cash" shows up, so in the security packet we'll spell out KMS and HSM details.
[01:43] Aaron Green: For data ingestion — our plan is to ship anonymized batches to S3 and also set up a streaming channel for incremental updates. We need to know how Redwood handles prefix caching and KV cache for partial conversations.
[01:57] Ben Cho: Good question. Runtime uses prefix and KV caching for repeated history to save tokens. We'll provide guidance on which keys to cache; we also have tooling for pre-warm and warm-up requests. Note: in some notes this got transcribed as "K V cache" which is the same thing — just spelling quirks.
[02:20] Priya Shah: Timeline — we're targeting a pilot in 30 days to validate latency and cost per inference. Success criteria: avg latency < 220ms for short chat flows, and cost under $0.004 per generated token equivalent — ballpark.
[02:36] Maya Ortega: That's reasonable for a dedicated setup with token batching. We'll create a proposal with expected throughput and cost estimates.
[02:44] Tom Reeves: Network questions — will we need VPC peering or can we use private link? Also what's egress like?
[02:52] Ben Cho: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink depending on cloud provider. Egress depends on model footprints — if you use a private deployment on-prem we limit egress to the control plane and all inference stays in your env. We'll send network diagrams.
[03:10] Lena Morales: Can you confirm SOC2 status and whether you provide SOC2 artifacts?
[03:16] Renee Park: Redwood is SOC2 Type II — we'll attach the compliance pack with the security packet. We'll also include evidence mapping for controls you asked about.
[03:26] Aaron Green: Any guidance for embedding pipelines? We plan to use embeddings for search and reranking.
[03:33] Ben Cho: Embeddings are supported; recommendation is to run embeddings in a batch job to build your vector DB then use incremental updates. We'll include best-practices for dimensionality, quantization profiles, and when to use our Optimize suggestions.
[03:54] Priya Shah: Are there any gotchas around quantized models and inference variance? We care about stability of outputs.
[04:02] Ben Cho: There can be slight numeric differences; our Optimize tool suggests quantization profiles by workload. For the pilot we can lock model version and quant profile to avoid regressions. Also we'll run evals against your prompt set.
[04:22] Maya Ortega: Ok, let's talk deliverables. We'll send: 1) activation runbook, 2) security pack and SOC2 artifacts, 3) a draft pricing/pilot quote, 4) DDI network diagram and onboarding checklist.
[04:37] Tom Reeves: Perfect. We want a data ingest workshop to walk through S3 permissions, IAM roles, and streaming connectors.
[04:45] Ben Cho: We'll schedule that. I can lead the data ingest workshop with Aaron; will cover S3 staging, streaming via Kinesis or Pub/Sub, and expected file formats.
[04:57] Priya Shah: Also need to know who on our side should be included in the bench tests — we'll include Tom and Aaron.
[05:04] Maya Ortega: Great — on next steps we'll set a 90-minute ingest workshop next week and a technical deep dive the week after if needed.
[05:13] Lena Morales: One more on audit logs — we want at least 90 days of logs forwarded to our SIEM and PII filtering on any logs you generate.
[05:23] Renee Park: We can route logs for 90 days; PII filtering will be part of the configuration. We'll include log retention options in the packet.
[05:34] Aaron Green: For credentials, do you support cross-account IAM roles for the S3 buckets?
[05:40] Ben Cho: Yes, cross-account roles are standard. We'll provide a sample policy.
[05:47] (inaudible chatter)
[06:10] Priya Shah: Wanted to surface a concern — we have internal procurement that needs a timeline for enterprise contract review. Can't be open-ended.
[06:18] Maya Ortega: Understood — we'll include a proposed SOW for the 30-day pilot and a timeline for enterprise review. Renee will coordinate with procurement.
[06:27] Renee Park: I'll send a procurement package and a checklist of items procurement typically asks for.
[06:33] Tom Reeves: Benchmarks — how do you run performance tests? We want to replicate our expected concurrency profile.
[06:41] Ben Cho: We can run a benchmark window against a dedicated pool; you'll provide a p95 sequence length distribution and concurrency. We can then size the dedicated capacity. We'll do 24–72 hour window to capture variance.
[06:55] Priya Shah: Any constraints on tokenization differences across models? We saw differences when we switched models in another vendor.
[07:03] Ben Cho: Tokenization differences exist; we'll lock the model and tokenizer for the pilot. Also we'll include a note on deterministic seeding for sampling if you want stable text outputs.
[07:18] [08:12] Maya Ortega: All right, quick recap before we run out of time — agreed items: runbook, security pack, network diagrams, data ingest workshop, pricing/pilot quote, and scheduling the benchmark window.
[08:35] Lena Morales: On encryption — do you support customer-managed keys in GCP and AWS?
[08:40] Ben Cho: Yes, CMKs in both clouds plus HSM options; on-prem we can integrate with your HSM. We'll detail the KMS flow in the security docs.
[08:52] Priya Shah: For the pilot, who is the day-to-day CSM?
[08:56] Renee Park: I'll be the CSM. I'll schedule weekly 30-minute syncs during the pilot and a biweekly exec summary with you.
[09:07] Aaron Green: Any gotchas around rate limiting during the benchmark? We want to avoid throttles mid-test.
[09:12] Ben Cho: We'll coordinate a temporary quota bump during the benchmark, and suggest using continuous batching to minimize tail latency.
[09:22] (overlap) Tom Reeves: Do you have a suggested retention policy for KV cache?
[09:27] Ben Cho: Usually a session-level cache with a TTL of 24 hours is common; but depends on session patterns. We'll include default config.
[09:37] Maya Ortega: I'll put together the timeline. Proposed: runbook & security docs by 2026-09-01, ingest workshop week of 2026-09-07, benchmark window week of 2026-09-14, and pilot review 2026-09-28. Does that work?
[09:58] Priya Shah: That aligns with our procurement window.
[10:03] Lena Morales: We'll review the SOC2 evidence as soon as you send it.
[10:08] Maya Ortega: Ok, final notes — we'll add small items: 1) sample IAM policy, 2) example cURL calls and SDK snippets for your data team, 3) an eval template to capture quality regressions. Links: Activation runbook: https://redwood.in/activation-runbook (will include attachments). Security packet: https://redwood.in/security-packet.
[10:32] (murmur)
[10:45] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone. Look forward to the ingest workshop.
[10:50] Maya Ortega: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the packet.
[10:55] (meeting ends)

Customer to share p95 sequence length distribution and concurrency profile for benchmark (by 2026-09-08)
SE to provision benchmark window and temporary quota bump (week of 2026-09-14)
CSM to coordinate procurement SOW & checklist with Oakmont procurement (Renee)
